item.title: Bauhaus Manifesto: Broad alliance promoting artistic freedom
item.description: Weeks before Saxony-Anhalt's state election, representatives from German cultural, crafts, architecture, design and church sectors unite to promote freedom, openness and creativity.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
item.description: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
item.description: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
item.description: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern Munich
item.description: Bernadette Amani is heading into her first full season with Bayern Munich, having joined the club in January. Making a living at football is something she never imagined possible while growing up in rural Ivory Coast.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
item.description: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala collapses on pitch again
item.description: One of Germany's top footballers has collapsed on the pitch for a second time in four days ahead of the new season. Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala has said he has a "neurological dysfunction" that causes blackouts.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
item.description: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
item.description: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
item.description: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Dressed for power: Giorgia Meloni and the language of fashion
item.description: From Giorgia Meloni's shift from dark suits to pastels to Angela Merkel's signature jackets, politicians have long used clothing to shape how voters see them. In this day and age, power dressing has evolved.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
item.description: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
item.description: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble
item.description: The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Can the cool north handle a surge in climate tourism?
item.description: With heat records continually being broken and southern summers getting hotter, travelers are heading north. Fragile ecosystems are paying the price.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Fatty food raises risk of colorectal cancer
item.description: Did you know fatty foods can increase production of an acid in your gut that promotes tumor growth? That's on top of all the other health risks linked to fatty foods, like fries and burgers.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
item.description: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
item.description: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?
item.description: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
item.description: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
item.description: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
item.description: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.
item.dc:subject: Science
